input: Create a personalized workout split for the next cycle

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of split (e.g., Push/Pull/Legs, Upper/Lower, Full Body, Body Part) fundamentally changes the structure of the entire plan.
The user's current training experience level (beginner, intermediate, advanced) dictates volume, intensity, and exercise complexity.
Where they train (home, commercial gym, garage gym) determines which equipment and exercises are actually available to them.
The number of days per week they can train is the single hardest limit that shapes the entire split structure.
Their primary goal (muscle gain, fat loss, strength, endurance, general fitness) determines how sessions are programmed — rep ranges, rest periods, intensity.
Knowing what a successful cycle looks like (e.g., hit a PR, improve a lagging muscle group, lose X lbs) defines how progress will be measured and what to prioritize.
How long each session can last affects how much volume can be packed in per day and whether accessory work is realistic.

gold.taskTitle: Create a personalized workout split for next cycle
gold.taskDescription: Design a structured, repeating workout schedule tailored to the user's fitness goals, available days, and training preferences for their upcoming training cycle.

questions.title: What is your primary goal for this training cycle?
questions.description: Understand whether the user is targeting muscle hypertrophy, strength gains, fat loss, improved endurance, or general fitness — this is the north star for all programming decisions.

questions.title: How many days per week can you commit to training?
questions.description: Determine the hard weekly availability limit, which directly dictates which split structures are even possible (e.g., 3-day vs. 5-day splits).

questions.title: How long have you been training consistently?
questions.description: Establish the user's experience level — beginner, intermediate, or advanced — to calibrate appropriate volume, intensity, and exercise selection.

questions.title: Where will you be doing most of your training?
questions.description: Identify the training environment (commercial gym, home gym, garage gym, bodyweight only) to ensure the split is built around actually available equipment.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred split style in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a preference for a specific structure such as Push/Pull/Legs, Upper/Lower, Full Body, or a body-part bro split, versus being open to a recommendation.

questions.title: How long can each workout session realistically last?
questions.description: Determine per-session time budget (e.g., 45 min, 60 min, 90 min) to know how much volume and how many exercises can fit into each day.

questions.title: What does a successful end to this cycle look like for you?
questions.description: Clarify the user's concrete success marker — hitting a specific lift PR, visibly improving a lagging body part, completing all sessions — to ensure the plan is built toward a measurable outcome.
